Title: Effect of resveratrol supplementation on metabolic risk markers and anthropometric parameters in individuals with obesity or overweight: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials - PMC
# Effect of resveratrol supplementation on metabolic risk markers and anthropometric parameters in individuals with obesity or overweight: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials. To address these gaps, this systematic review and meta-analysis seeks to integrate existing evidence on the effects of resveratrol supplementation on metabolic risk markers and anthropometric parameters in individuals with obesity or overweight, aiming to provide a comprehensive assessment of its efficacy and potential clinical applications. Both medical subject headings and free text words were used to search PubMed. The PICO criteria were used to screen the studies for this meta-analysis, with patients (P) being individuals with obesity or overweight; intervention (I) being the use of resveratrol supplementations; control (C) being patients receiving placebo, no treatment, or usual care; and outcomes (O) delineated by our PICO criteria involve a thorough examination of how resveratrol influences a range of biochemical and anthropometric parameters, specifically assessing its effects on biochemical markers such as triglycerides, total cholesterol levels, HbA1c, insulin, as well as liver enzymes such as AST and ALT. The criteria for inclusion in our analysis were diligently established as follows: (i) randomized controlled trials that juxtapose the efficacy of resveratrol treatment against a placebo, (ii) studies involving participants who are classified as individuals with obesity or overweight, (iii) trials in which participants were free from significant comorbid conditions, (iv) trials where participants were not undergoing any concurrent treatments that could potentially influence glucose metabolism or homeostasis, (v) for studies showing a crossover design, only data from the initial randomization phase were used, owing to potential concerns regarding carryover effects, (vi) only those randomized controlled trials whose results directly addressed our specified efficacy outcomes were incorporated into the meta-analysis. To study the impact of resveratrol supplementation on participants’ HbA1c levels, data from three studies , , ] involving 87 patients was extracted and statistically analyzed, yielding the following results (SMD = 0.00, 95%CI [−0.99, 1.00], P = 0.99, I2 = 80 %), (high certainty) as shown in Fig. 4(c). This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the effects of resveratrol supplementation on various metabolic risk markers and anthropometric parameters in Individuals with Obesity or Overweight.
